findings.governingReading: Shirou has prepared chicken drumettes, the meaty lower wing sections.
findings.explanation: The English broadens the ingredient to wings.

findings.governingReading: The curry-flavored sauce is for sardine kabayaki.
findings.explanation: The English drops the prepared dish and leaves plain sardines.

findings.governingReading: Sakura praises Shirou’s clever idea for making fish approachable.
findings.explanation: The English turns situational ingenuity into general intelligence.

findings.governingReading: Sakura offers to clean and break down the fish.
findings.explanation: “Cut” loses the culinary operation.

findings.governingReading: Shirou is to check the simmered dishes already cooking.
findings.explanation: The English makes the object an abstract process.

findings.governingReading: Sakura is asked to scrape away the sardine’s belly bones.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes a central spine-like bone.

findings.evidenceJa: 弾むように言って、桜はいそいそと
findings.governingReading: Sakura speaks buoyantly and moves eagerly toward the refrigerator.
findings.explanation: The English deletes both signs of her good mood.

findings.governingReading: Shirou enjoys cooking with a partner who anticipates and supports his intent.
findings.explanation: The English removes the partner term connecting kitchen coordination to the later household proposal.

findings.highlight: Sushi chef, your hands aren’t moving
findings.evidenceJa: お寿司屋さん、止まってます
findings.governingReading: Sakura jokes that the “sushi chef” himself has stopped while distracted.
findings.explanation: The English redirects the joke to his hands, awkwardly salient because his left hand is already immobile.

findings.highlight: I sigh so she can’t see
findings.evidenceJa: 桜に気付かれないように息をついて
findings.governingReading: Shirou sighs while trying to keep Sakura from noticing by any sense.
findings.explanation: The English oddly makes a sigh something she must not see.

findings.evidenceJa: かろうじて調理できる食材
findings.governingReading: Soft sardines are barely within Shirou’s one-handed ability.
findings.explanation: The English drops the narrow margin.

findings.highlight: cutting apart a cow with a kitchen knife
findings.evidenceJa: 包丁一本で牛バラしたり
findings.governingReading: His example of technique is butchering a cow with only one knife.
findings.explanation: The English omits the one-tool extremity.

findings.governingReading: The contrasting feat is producing an ice sculpture in one swift, clean flourish.
findings.explanation: The English deletes the comic sound and speed.

findings.highlight: We’ll cook it after you’re done
findings.governingReading: They will grill the sardines after Sakura removes the belly bones.
findings.explanation: The English omits the specific remaining task.

findings.evidenceJa: サラダ油をこさじ半分ほど
findings.governingReading: Shirou adds approximately half a teaspoon of cooking oil.
findings.explanation: The English drops both oil type and measured quantity.

findings.evidenceJa: フライパンを持つ手が止まった
findings.governingReading: The hand holding the frying pan freezes at Sakura’s question.
findings.explanation: The English omits the pan that makes the reaction visible and potentially risky.

findings.highlight: I’m sure Sakura didn’t see my disturbance
findings.evidenceJa: 伝わらなかっただろう
findings.governingReading: Shirou supposes his one-instant reaction probably did not register with Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English strengthens probability and narrows perception to sight.

findings.evidenceJa: その代わりに、俺は何が出来て
findings.governingReading: With Illya’s original purpose already gone, Shirou wonders what he can do instead.
findings.explanation: The English explicitly casts him as replacing Kiritsugu.

findings.evidenceJa: うちに住んでもらっちゃダメかな
findings.governingReading: Shirou asks whether Illya may live in their home if she does not return abroad.
findings.explanation: “Stay” leaves the long-term household proposal temporary.

findings.governingReading: Shirou mistakenly worries that Sakura’s fever has flared back up.
findings.explanation: The English sounds like a separate new fever.

findings.governingReading: Shirou believes proper, open conversation can let Sakura and Illya get along.
findings.explanation: The English drops the qualitative condition.

findings.governingReading: The written future carries “wish” as its reading, fusing a hoped-for household future with desire.
findings.explanation: The English retains wish but loses the written future layer.

findings.governingReading: Because Sakura also saw Rin, Shirou jokes that the apparition was not a hallucination.
findings.explanation: The English normalizes the joke to imagination.

findings.governingReading: The narration comically presents morning Rin as an unidentified strange thing.
findings.explanation: The English immediately resolves the objectified presence as a person.

findings.governingReading: Rin thumps down and roughly claims her place.
findings.explanation: The English invents a shambling gait and omits her forceful occupation of the seat.

findings.governingReading: Rin pours tea and turns on the television, each action separately marked by apparent ill humor.
findings.explanation: The English compresses the repeated presentation into one glower.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka and Illya sit across from us
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂とイリヤが隣り合う
findings.governingReading: The text establishes two adjacent pairs without explicitly stating that the pairs face each other.
findings.explanation: The English invents the across-table relation.

findings.governingReading: Illya condescendingly praises Sakura’s refined seasoning.
findings.explanation: “Taste” can describe palate or flavor and loses the act of seasoning.

findings.highlight: I usually don’t eat in the morning
findings.governingReading: Rin claims a personal rule or policy of not eating breakfast while already eating.
findings.explanation: The English changes the comic contradiction from principle to habit.

findings.evidenceJa: かわるがわる新しい話題
findings.governingReading: The noisy television successively supplies one new topic after another.
findings.explanation: The English is unnatural and loses alternation and novelty.

findings.governingReading: The discoverer encounters the scene during his habitual morning run.
findings.explanation: The English omits that it is his daily routine.

findings.governingReading: The report identifies a man at the threshold of old age or late middle age.
findings.explanation: The English makes him straightforwardly old.

findings.evidenceJa: 被害者のものと思われる遺体の一部
findings.governingReading: Police reportedly find part of a body thought to belong to the victim.
findings.explanation: The English pluralizes victims before the report establishes the possible count.

findings.governingReading: The shadow had previously drained magical energy from the town’s residents.
findings.explanation: The English drops the town-wide population relation.

findings.governingReading: From Shirou’s knowledge, it should not previously have killed people directly in this manner.
findings.explanation: The English turns his expectation into categorical history.

findings.highlight: I’m sure this was an unforeseen accident
findings.evidenceJa: 事故だったんじゃないかしら
findings.governingReading: Rin tentatively proposes an unforeseen accident as her preferred explanation.
findings.explanation: The English promotes the hypothesis into certainty.

findings.highlight: omelet is gone as she speaks
findings.evidenceJa: 卵焼きはとっくになくなっている
findings.governingReading: Rin’s own omelet has long since been eaten before she offers the wager.
findings.explanation: The English suggests it becomes gone during her speech.

findings.governingReading: Rin infers the shadow fed by itself without Zouken present.
findings.explanation: The English frames exclusivity around what ate at the scene rather than the shadow acting independently.

findings.highlight: there was four of something people only have one of
findings.evidenceJa: 一つしかない筈のものが四つ
findings.governingReading: Rin posits four examples of a body part each person should possess only once.
findings.explanation: The English uses singular “was” with four objects and awkwardly attaches the relative clause.

findings.governingReading: Such shapes could establish victim count even before forensic examination.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes identification of persons for forensic analysis of evidence.
